Sheet 02 — Orthographic

Two plates, twelve anchors,
two module bays.

Every hole in this enclosure is placed against a real board footprint. The floor carries three separate four-point patterns; the lid carries two windows that let the display and the sensor face the outside world.

01

5 mm walls throughout

Heavy for an electronics box, and deliberately so — the shell is stiff enough to be handled at outreach events without flexing against the boards.

02

140 × 140 × 45 mm cavity

Enough clear volume to stack all three MYOSA boards side by side with their JST leads routed between them.

03

Side cable pass-through

A single rectangular cut-out in one wall, aligned with the ESP32 carrier's USB-C receptacle, so the unit charges and flashes closed.

Sheet 03 — What goes inside

One bus. Three boards.
Everything daisy-chains.

MYOSA boards share a single I²C bus. Each carrier breaks out SCL / SDA / GND / VCC on both edges, so modules chain end to end instead of fanning back to the controller.

Bay — internal

ESP32 carrier

The controller board never breaks the lid surface. It mounts to the tall four-point pattern on the floor and reaches the outside only through the side cut-out.

Sheet 05 — Where it goes

Built to be carried,
opened and explained.

This is teaching hardware. The enclosure exists so a bare I²C stack survives a bag, a demo table and thirty pairs of hands.

Outreach

Chapter demos

A closed, labelled unit that reads as a finished instrument on a stand, instead of loose boards on a breadboard.

Laboratory

Bench sensing

Colour, gesture and proximity capture with the readout on the lid, so no laptop is needed to see live values.

Coursework

Firmware teaching

Students flash over USB-C without opening the case — the pass-through keeps the assembly intact through a whole lab session.

Sheet 06 — Colophon

Designed by an
IEEE IAS member.

The enclosure was modelled as a two-part assembly in Autodesk Inventor 2027. Every render on this page was generated straight from that assembly — the same solid the printer is fed.
